title: review: H5b fix round 3: the review re-spawn capacity check reuses free_slots' Claude-worker counting (assigned_to or executor starting claude:) instead of a duplicate that omits the executor marker (review T-0399)
spec:
STEP 0: the worktree must contain ec54196, 3164bed, f7df4d7 and a553af1 (T-0363, T-0393, T-0396) in git log; never drop or amend them.
Review T-0399 on T-0396, one finding:
1. (med) orchestrator/daemon.py:551 the review re-spawn capacity check counts running Claude workers by assigned_to starting with claude: only; free_slots (daemon.py:454-475) deliberately counts assigned_to OR executor starting with claude: (gotchas T-0070: a Claude-fallback execute task carries the marker on executor). The duplicate omits that case, so re-spawns can push concurrent Claude workers above [limits].max_parallel_claude_workers. Fix: extract the running-Claude-worker count from free_slots into one helper (running_claude_workers(pool)) and use it in both free_slots and the re-spawn check, including in-flight dispatches exactly as free_slots does; no second counting logic remains. Test: tests/test_daemon.py::test_respawn_counts_claude_fallback_executors (a running execute task with executor claude:sonnet and assigned_to codex consumes a Claude slot; with max_parallel_claude_workers reached, no review is re-spawned).
Keep the T-0363, T-0393 and T-0396 tests green. Run .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh from the worktree root until it exits 0, then git add -A and git commit with the task id; report sha and failures only.
acceptance: git log --oneline in the worktree shows a553af1, f7df4d7, 3164bed and ec54196 below your commit
one helper counts running Claude workers and both free_slots and the re-spawn path call it (grep shows a single startswith('claude:') counting site)
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

comments.issue: The respawn loop for review/spec_review tasks stamps respawned_at and calls spawn_async(spawn.run_worker, task_id) inside bus.locked() without re-checking that the task's status is still 'queued'. The outer bus.read(status='queued') snapshot can go stale between iteration and lock acquisition: if the original spawn thread was merely slow (not dead) and calls bus.claim in that window, this loop still dispatches a second run_worker for the same task_id. Both workers then race on ensure_worktree's unlocked 'git worktree add' for the same task branch/dir and can both call bus.post_result, with the second overwriting the first's verdict (spawn.py's parse_failed/existing_result guard only protects an already-posted result at check time, not a concurrent in-flight post). Add `if current.get('status') != 'queued': continue` inside the lock before spawning.

Unlike the execute-dispatch loop above it (which skips stale(t)), this new review/spec_review respawn loop never checks stale(task), so it can respawn a review whose parent goal is already done, wasting an account turn on moot work.
